_comment: THE canonical version-matrix construct catalogue (VERSION_TEST_MATRIX_DESIGN.md §10 #5). Each entry: a minimal program exercising ONE construct + its edition metadata. VersionMatrixTests computes the expected outcome per (construct × edition): compiles iff introducedIn <= V and (removedIn null or V < removedIn). The human-readable VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md and the in-code ConstructDialectStatus registry are renderings of THIS file — extend it here, never fork. 'vcr' cites the VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row/section or the introducing standard where the doc has no row (it covers 2002→2023 deltas only). OPTIONAL 'status': 'pending' = catalogued (edition metadata frozen by the drift tests) but not yet implemented — the matrix SKIPS its compile assertions until the owning roadmap phase lands and flips it active (the one pending mechanism, shared with the corpus discovery manifests). Vendor-dialect constructs live in vendor-constructs.json (owner decision 2), never here.

constructs.description: Nucleus MOVE/DISPLAY — edition-invariant since COBOL-85
constructs.vcr: baseline (no row — never changed)
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. NUC.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 W PIC X(5) VALUE "HI".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    MOVE "BYE" TO W.
    DISPLAY W.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.description: ALLOCATE statement (dynamic storage), ISO §14.9.3 - introduced 2002. ACTIVE as of Phase-4b increment 2 (DEVLOG 617): both formats bind (n CHARACTERS RETURNING p -> a fresh StorageCell window pointer, GR1 round-up / GR2 <=0 -> NULL no EC / GR6 INITIALIZED zero-fill; based-item -> the implicit pointer takes a cell of the template width, GR3/GR4); the based INITIALIZED GR7 INITIALIZE lowering is a named staged residue.

constructs.description: FREE statement (release ALLOCATEd storage), ISO §14.9.15 - introduced 2002. ACTIVE as of Phase-4b increment 2 (DEVLOG 617): per-operand GR1 three-way (release-and-null / NULL no-op / nonfatal EC-STORAGE-NOT-ALLOC through the TurnState-gated status block); SR1 data-pointer operands only (the vendor FREE based-item form rejects 0869); a freed cell's dangling aliases fail loud at the next dereference (EC-BOUND-PTR).

constructs.description: INVOKE (OO method call), ISO §14.9.23 — introduced 2002. LIVE since the Phase-3 spine part 2 (DEVLOG 601): Class NEW RETURNING → new C(); no-arg instance INVOKE → virtual call behind the EC-OO-NULL guard (§14.9.23.4 GR5); USING/RETURNING marshaling (slice 2), SELF/SUPER (3b), factory and universal dispatch stage loud. Below 2002 the grammar gate + W1.5 mapping name the edition (0900).

constructs.description: EXIT FUNCTION statement - introduced 2002 with user-defined functions, REMOVED 2023 (Annex E :49036; dual-obligation window: 0900 below 2002 via expectDiagnosticBelow, 0902 at 2023). ACTIVE as of Phase 4c (DEVLOG 616): the binder realizes the function-return synonym (UdfBindExitFunction -> BoundGoback, the 14.9.18.4 GR5 semantics) with the 0827 placement band (only in a function definition); the conforming witness is a whole-source caller + FUNCTION-ID unit (the udf_exit_function golden proves the early-return behavior X=0014). At 85 the {is2002()}? PD-header RETURNING parse hint names the edition (0900).

constructs.description: ENTER statement (X3.23-1985 Nucleus: ENTER language-name [routine-name]) - other-language entry, comment-equivalent when only COBOL is supported (bound BoundNop at 85; the operands are SYSTEM-names, deliberately not cobolWord - ENTER COBOL is conforming '85 source and COBOL is an '85 reserved word); deleted by ISO 2002.

constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMEN1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 W PIC 9 VALUE 7.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    ENTER LINKAGE.
    DISPLAY W.
    ENTER COBOL.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.description: USE FOR DEBUGGING declarative (the '85 debug facility) - deleted by ISO 2002 with the whole facility (DEBUG-* registers included). Accepted-inert at 85: without WITH DEBUGGING MODE the debugging section is compiled as if comment lines (the '85 rule); with it, compiled but never triggered (the object-time switch is permanently off). Companion of debugging-mode-removed-2002.
constructs.vcr: VCR Table 7 row 7.17; the W3 notInGrammar 85-acceptance batch (DEVLOG 599)

IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. VMUD1.

constructs.description: Section-header segment-number (the '85 Segmentation module: section-name SECTION [0-99].; 50-99 = independent segments) - parsed-and-ignored at 85 (all segments resident, a conforming posture; the independent-segment ALTER-reversion rules are deliberately not implemented - ALTER is itself gated 0810/0811); deleted by ISO 2002. Companion of segment-limit-removed-2002.

constructs.description: User-defined function reference FUNCTION function-prototype-name(args) - ISO §8.4.3.2 function-identifier / §9.4 user-defined functions / §12.3.8.2 GR12 (a REPOSITORY-declared name refers to the user function, never a same-named intrinsic). LIVE (Phase 4c M2-UDF-1, DEVLOG 615): in-group whole-source activation lowered onto the program-activation ABI - a hoisted CALL...RETURNING over an §8.4.3.2.4 GR1 result temporary; args in the §8.4.3.2.4 GR5 manner (identifier BY REFERENCE, literal/arith-expr private copy). Below 2002 the binder gate names the edition (0900); the {is2002()}?-gated PD-header RETURNING parse hint fires there too (procedure-returning-2002).
constructs.vcr: M2 UDF catalog (PHASE4_RECONCILIATION M2-UDF-1); unblocks M2-UDF-2 (folds in) + EXIT FUNCTION (M2-PROC-6)
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. UFMX1.
ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
CONFIGURATION SECTION.
REPOSITORY.
    FUNCTION UFMXDBL.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 W PIC 9(4).
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    COMPUTE W = FUNCTION UFMXDBL(21).
    STOP RUN.
END PROGRAM UFMX1.
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
FUNCTION-ID. UFMXDBL.
DATA DIVISION.
LINKAGE SECTION.
01 L-X PIC 9(4).
01 L-R PIC 9(4).
PROCEDURE DIVISION USING L-X RETURNING L-R.
P.
    COMPUTE L-R = L-X * 2.
    GOBACK.
END FUNCTION UFMXDBL.

constructs.description: SET ADDRESS OF (data-pointer assignment), ISO §14.9.39 Format 7 + §8.4.3.11 ADDRESS OF - introduced 2002. LIVE (Phase-4b increment 2, DEVLOG 617): both directions - SET p TO ADDRESS OF x (the sender form; x's record is forced onto a StorageCell so a CellPointer window can alias it) and SET ADDRESS OF b TO p (SR18 - the receiver shall be BASED; GR12-13 snapshot assignment). Binder-side registry gate (a grammar predicate would fall through to the other SET alternatives and mis-diagnose).
constructs.vcr: 2002 introduction (derive from the 2002 standard - Annex E covers 2014-2023 only)
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. SAMX1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 X PIC X(5) VALUE "HELLO".
01 P USAGE POINTER.
01 B PIC X(5) BASED.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    SET P TO ADDRESS OF X.
    SET ADDRESS OF B TO P.
    STOP RUN.

constructs.description: SET pointer UP/DOWN BY (data-pointer arithmetic), ISO §14.9.39 Format 10 - introduced 2002 (GR20 byte-granular movement; GR18 NULL -> EC-DATA-PTR-NULL; GR19: a non-integer amount VALUE is a runtime EC-SIZE-ADDRESS fatal via CobolPtr.UpByScaled - the exact value rule, never a silent truncation). LIVE (Phase-4b increment 2, DEVLOG 617): the D-U7 category re-route on the shared 85 index grammar shape - the 85 index form itself stays ungated.
constructs.vcr: 2002 introduction (derive from the 2002 standard - Annex E covers 2014-2023 only)
constructs.source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. PAMX1.
DATA DIVISION.
WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
01 X PIC X(5) VALUE "HELLO".
01 P USAGE POINTER.
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    SET P TO ADDRESS OF X.
    SET P UP BY 2.
    STOP RUN.
